problem: Federated learning degrades under data heterogeneity and distribution shifts when using local feature statistics for test-time adaptation.
approach: FedPAT learns a global prototype affinity topology (the relational structure among class prototypes) by aggregating from source clients, then uses topology-aware diffusion and optimization for test-time adaptation on unseen target clients.
contribution: FedPAT consistently outperforms federated and classical test-time adaptation methods across various distribution shifts by leveraging stable prototype relationships.

problem: Federated learning deletion requests require client-level unlearning, but client influence is deeply entangled after aggregation, making unlearning slow and unstable.
approach: Influence-Disentangled Federated Training decomposes each round's updates into shared covarying directions and client-separable residual traces, using entanglement-aware shrinkage to suppress non-removable components.
contribution: IDFT achieves deletion with a single subtraction and short repair, attaining the lowest retrain gap and improving the fidelity-cost frontier on multiple benchmarks.

problem: LLM agents struggle with multi-step reasoning over FHIR-structured clinical graphs, often selecting wrong resources or violating traversal constraints.
approach: A CodeAct agent is post-trained with reinforcement learning using a custom harness, tools, and LLM Judge providing execution-grounded rewards over the queryable FHIR graph.
contribution: RL post-training improves answer correctness from 50% to 77% on FHIR-AgentBench using a smaller, cheaper Qwen3-8B model while enforcing data-integrity constraints.

problem: Existing relational learning methods use static entity representations and assume symmetric inference, inadequate for capturing context-dependent functions and asymmetric high-order relations.
approach: CONTEXTOR decomposes high-order relations into incomplete query tuples and response entities, contextualizing candidate responses via asymmetric conditional modulation and aligning via multi-fold contrastive learning.
contribution: CONTEXTOR consistently outperforms existing methods on benchmark datasets across diverse biomedical tasks.

problem: Neural networks are nonlinear, making classical linear algebra tools (SVD, projection, etc.) inapplicable to nonlinear mappings.
approach: The Linearizer framework identifies non-standard vector spaces where a neural network acts as a linear operator by sandwiching it between invertible networks, using transport of structure to derive custom addition and scaling.
contribution: Diffusion model sampling collapses from hundreds of steps into a single step; the framework also enables idempotency enforcement and modular style transfer.

problem: Multimodal LLMs for document understanding degrade under real-world degradations (noise, blur, low resolution) due to scarcity of large-scale training data and lack of transferable solutions across architectures.
approach: Uni-DocRobust proposes a universal plug-and-play framework with a frozen Universal Restoration Core trained via multi-teacher distillation in canonical feature space, integrated via lightweight Feature Adapters into target MLLMs.
contribution: With DocRobust-VQA (189K clean/corrupted pairs, 417K QA pairs), Uni-DocRobust significantly enhances robust MLLM performance across architectures via a cost-effective pre-train-once-deploy-everywhere paradigm.

problem: Multi-headed self-attention has a large memory footprint, motivating specialized low-rank factorizations like GQA and MLA, but their theoretical foundations and parameter efficiency trade-offs are unclear.
approach: Tucker Attention generalizes GQA and MLA via a unified low-rank factorization strategy across embedding dimensions and attention heads, constructing a parameter-efficient scheme compatible with flash-attention and RoPE.
contribution: Tucker Attention requires an order of magnitude fewer parameters than GQA and MLA for comparable performance on LLMs and ViTs while encompassing them as special cases.

problem: SVD-based delta compression for fine-tuned LLM parameters lacks principled quantization, leading to poor generalizability and storage/distribution challenges.
approach: PrinMix models quantization as an optimization problem via 0/1 Integer Linear Programming, deriving quantization error theory and identifying singular-value-dominated scaling that necessitates mixed-precision quantization, with Reconstruction Target Correction for sequential quantization errors.
contribution: PrinMix outperforms SOTA Delta-CoMe by 22.3% on AIME2024 and 6.1% on GQA for 7B LLM compression.

problem: Enforcing measurement or physics consistency in inverse problems with diffusion models typically relies on heuristic guidance or task-specific training with limited feasibility guarantees.
approach: Terminal-conditioned inversion constructs a backward stochastic differential equation whose adapted solution defines a principled inverse map from terminal feasibility specifications to prior states, with a practical neural BSDE solver.
contribution: The framework achieves improved sparse-view CT reconstruction quality over training-free baselines while guaranteeing strict measurement feasibility under prescribed terminal specifications.

problem: Boltzmann Generators for molecular sampling face scalability limits, and coarse-grained surrogates lack reweighting procedures to ensure correct statistics.
approach: Coarse-Grained Boltzmann Generators use a flow-based model in reduced coordinate space and reweight via a learned potential of mean force, with the PMF learned from rapidly converged enhanced-sampling trajectories.
contribution: CG-BGs capture solvent-mediated interactions in highly reduced representations while substantially reducing computational cost relative to atomistic Boltzmann Generators.

problem: Sequential editing of structured knowledge in LLMs relies on complex regularization mechanisms whose necessity is unclear, and stability under accumulating edits remains unprincipled.
approach: Via optimization analysis, the work establishes formal equivalence between one-time and sequential editing, generalizing to a broader class of objectives and showing stability emerges from properly accounting for accumulated constraints rather than specialized regularization.
contribution: The framework simplifies sequential knowledge editing, eliminates unnecessary regularization strategies, and robustly handles conflicting edits while maintaining consistent behavior.

problem: Constrained saddle-point problems require projection onto feasible sets which is computationally expensive; existing projection-free methods lack unified analysis across nonconvex-concave settings.
approach: A unified dual dynamic smoothing framework enables efficient single-loop algorithms using linear minimization oracles with anytime convergence guarantees not requiring pre-specified iteration horizons.
contribution: The framework provides unified analysis for nonconvex-concave and nonconvex-strongly concave settings, significantly narrowing the performance gap between projection-free and projection-based methods.

problem: Multimodal LLMs suffer from object hallucinations driven by attention distraction, where spatial inconsistency in multi-head attention and temporal fading of visual tokens during decoding cause inaccurate descriptions.
approach: AFIP corrects attention distraction via cross-head attention enrichment and reinforces visual grounding through dynamic historical attention enhancement, without requiring additional training.
contribution: AFIP reduces hallucinations by addressing the underlying attention mechanism across multiple benchmarks and models.

problem: Combining multiple self-supervised learning objectives on graphs causes interference, training instability, and three failure modes: disagreement, drift, and drought.
approach: ControlG recasts multi-objective graph SSL as feedback-controlled temporal allocation, estimating per-objective difficulty and pairwise antagonism, planning budgets via Pareto-aware log-hypervolume, and scheduling with a PID controller.
contribution: ControlG consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across 9 datasets while producing auditable schedules revealing which objectives drove learning.

problem: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning for dense prediction tasks exhibits input-agnostic modeling and redundant cross-layer representations, limiting adaptation quality.
approach: ParaX employs a mixture-of-experts adapter with shared expert centers; during forward pass, each module dynamically generates tailored weight matrices via dynamic parameter routing that selectively aggregates parameter matrices.
contribution: ParaX achieves superior performance across diverse visual recognition tasks by enabling low-rank input-dependent adaptation and promoting cross-layer feature interaction.

problem: Conventional autoregressive MLLMs limit architectural alternatives; discrete diffusion models show promise for NLP but have not been applied to unified multimodal understanding and generation.
approach: Omni-Diffusion is the first any-to-any multimodal model built on mask-based discrete diffusion, directly capturing the joint distribution over discrete multimodal tokens for text, speech, and images.
contribution: Omni-Diffusion outperforms or matches existing multimodal systems on diverse benchmarks, demonstrating significant promise of diffusion models for next-generation multimodal foundation models.

problem: Continual learning is vulnerable to data poisoning attacks that trigger divergence or severe excess risk, yet a principled theoretical foundation for attack and defense is lacking.
approach: Framing adversary-defender interaction as an online zero-sum game, the work establishes performance limits, proposes task-to-task verification for infrequent attacks, and derives robust defense minimizing sensitivity to poisoned features.
contribution: The framework proves no defense succeeds against linear-proportion task poisoning, but identifies defensible regimes and provides verified convergence guarantees for robust defense.

problem: Large multimodal models achieve high scores on existing visual benchmarks, quickly eroding headroom and making it hard to benchmark progress on visual reasoning over time.
approach: ZeroBench is a lightweight visual reasoning benchmark curated via adversarial filtering to be initially impossible for frontier LMMs, tracking progress year-over-year with human baseline comparison.
contribution: Initial SotA was 0% pass@1, reaching 19% pass@5 after one year; ZeroBench demonstrates sustained benchmark difficulty and charts progress on 46 LMMs.

problem: CAD generation as sequence modeling lacks intermediate visual feedback, hindering association of individual tokens with their geometric effects.
approach: An Argument-induced 3D Point Loss maps argument tokens to corresponding 3D points for dense token-wise geometric supervision, and a Grammar-constrained Operator leverages structured CAD program syntax to regulate generation.
contribution: The approach improves generation accuracy and program validity across five CAD tasks with diverse input modalities (text, SVG, point clouds, CAD sequences).

problem: Large-scale web-harvested datasets suffer from noisy correspondence in cross-modal retrieval, degrading generalization; existing methods rely on discrete selection inducing fragility and discretization error.
approach: IN2R shifts from discrete substitution to synthesizing a reliable soft prototype via graph-based intra-modal reasoning over neighbors, leveraging intrinsic geometric stability of intra-modal data.
contribution: IN2R synthesizes continuous soft prototypes reflecting local semantic consensus on Flickr30K, MS-COCO, and CC152K, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Machine learning training under fully homomorphic encryption lacks theoretical convergence analysis and relies on costly per-sample gradient clipping for privacy.
approach: Theoretical convergence analysis of approximate gradient descent via polynomial approximations, integrated with differential privacy without per-sample clipping, plus data-independent hyperparameter selection and theoretically grounded polynomial approximation strategies.
contribution: The work advances feasibility of efficient, private, and secure machine learning on sensitive data with proven convergence guarantees.

problem: Exploration in visual reinforcement learning under sparse rewards struggles due to task-irrelevant variations; existing methods assume low-dimensional states or lack task-aware strategies.
approach: TEB couples task-relevant representations with exploration via a predictive bisimulation metric that measures global intrinsic novelty, with a predicted reward differential term preventing representation collapse.
contribution: TEB achieves superior exploration ability on MetaWorld and Maze2D, outperforming recent baselines through task-aware novelty measurement.

problem: Generative sequence modeling faces tension between Transformer expressivity and linear sequence model efficiency; iterative methods like Test-Time Training break hardware parallelism due to serial dependencies.
approach: PRISM reconstructs the gate × residual × direction iteration pattern of TTT in parallelizable form via Write-Forget Decoupling and a two-stage proxy architecture (short-convolution anchoring and learned predictor for refinement).
contribution: PRISM achieves comparable performance to explicit optimization while delivering 174x higher throughput via parallelizable feedforward operations.

problem: High-fidelity stock market simulation must balance structural and behavioral fidelity; existing approaches face persistent trade-offs in capturing complex market dynamics from heterogeneous participants.
approach: MarketSim simulates over 15,000 heterogeneous LLM agents in a hierarchical architecture decoupling strategy from execution, operating in nanosecond-resolution continuous double auction, grounded in 12k real news/policy/earnings documents.
contribution: MarketSim captures key complexity properties of real markets and outperforms baselines in tracking high-frequency price dynamics with 3.48% average MAPE.

problem: Deep networks exhibit simplicity bias aiding generalization, but a broadly applicable quantitative measure of simplicity remains elusive.
approach: Polynomial representations approximate network behavior along data-dependent interpolation paths using orthogonal polynomial bases, with effective degree serving as a distribution-aware simplicity metric.
contribution: Effective degree is predictive of generalization across tasks and architectures, outperforming sharpness; polynomial-based simplicity regularization improves generalization in classification, fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning.

problem: Merging vision-language models with reasoning models at coarse-grained layer level trades off reasoning capability gain against visual capability loss.
approach: FRISM performs fine-grained reasoning injection via subspace-level model merging, decomposing LRM task vectors via SVD and adaptively tuning scaling coefficients per subspace through label-free self-distillation with dual-objective optimization.
contribution: FRISM effectively improves reasoning while largely preserving visual capabilities across diverse visual-language reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Evaluating long-form text-to-video generation under complex textual inputs with hierarchical metadata remains a significant challenge.
approach: LoCoT2V-Bench provides a benchmark for long video generation from multi-scene prompts with hierarchical metadata, plus LoCoT2V-Eval, a multi-dimensional framework covering perceptual quality, text-video alignment, temporal and dynamic quality, and HERD metric.
contribution: Experiments on 17 LVG models reveal strong perceptual quality but weak fine-grained text-video alignment and character consistency, identifying key challenges.

problem: Graph-based RAG over-relies on entity-centric node matching and lacks explicit causal modeling, leading to unfaithful or spurious answers; prior causality work is limited to local contexts.
approach: CausalRAG2 rethinks knowledge organization through causal gating across hierarchical modules, explicitly modeling causal relationships to suppress spurious correlations while enabling scalable cross-module reasoning over large-scale KGs.
contribution: CausalRAG2 consistently outperforms competitive graph-based RAG baselines on multiple datasets, establishing a principled foundation for structured, scalable, and causally grounded RAG.

problem: Existing 3D generation from single images is limited by restricted representation resolution, making them unsuitable for high-quality 3D scene generation.
approach: HIVE-3D introduces a hierarchical voxel enhancement framework: coarse initial scene, image segmentation and attention-based retrieval to align 2D/3D components, organizing relations into a component tree, then performing coarse-to-fine hierarchical voxel super-resolution.
contribution: HIVE-3D achieves state-of-the-art performance generating high-resolution, high-quality 3D scenes from single scene images.

problem: Text-to-image diffusion models memorize training data; existing mitigation via weight pruning fails to prevent replication when text embeddings are perturbed, revealing fragility of local assumptions.
approach: The work demonstrates memorization is not inherently local: replication triggers are distributed throughout embedding space, pruned models still leak via perturbed prompts, and different pruning methods identify inconsistent weights.
contribution: Findings enable more robust mitigation through adversarial fine-tuning and inform development of more reliable defenses against DM memorization.

problem: Existing dimensionality reduction methods preserve specific invariants but lack a unified approach based on preserving point-distribution similarity across reduction.
approach: A new invariant—point-distributions similarity—is proposed with a linear, efficient method achieving dimensionality reduction while preserving this invariant.
contribution: Theoretical feasibility is proven; benchmark and single-cell expression data demonstrate effectiveness and efficiency.

problem: Time series foundation models rely on large-scale diverse pretraining, yet temporal pattern heterogeneity across domains hinders effective learning of transferable representations.
approach: Olivia harmonizes datasets via normalized power spectral density in the spectral domain; a Harmonizer module reshapes spectral structures and implicitly harmonizes PSDs, mediated by a low-dimensional HarmonicAttention design.
contribution: Olivia consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance on TSLib, GIFT-Eval, and GluonTS under zero-shot, few-shot, and full-shot forecasting scenarios.

problem: Vision-language models exhibit asymmetric confusion on downstream data and suffer from Base-New Trade-off: improving unseen class performance degrades known class accuracy.
approach: NeRP is a plug-and-play prompting correction strategy using neutral text prompts and reference images to measure class-wise prior preferences along pre-trained geometry, correcting prior-dominated mispredictions via local class-pair flips.
contribution: NeRP substantially improves accuracy on unseen classes without parameter modification across 15 few-shot and cross-domain benchmarks.

problem: Continual release of aggregates (MaxSum, MinSum, MaxSelect, MinSelect) under differential privacy inherently admits large additive error.
approach: Algorithms allowing relative error are proposed for non-adaptive streams, with proven separation between non-adaptive and adaptive stream regimes.
contribution: The work shows error can be substantially reduced via relative terms under non-adaptive streams while proving adaptive streams admit unavoidable large error for selection tasks.

problem: Modeling learning curves for cost-effective data collection is difficult; most parametric methods are inappropriate when no reliable form exists, and GP approaches struggle with monotonicity constraints.
approach: MOVE introduces a monotonic variational GP with virtual-derivative factors enabling tractable posterior inference, and develops an expected shortfall objective for target-driven data collection.
contribution: MOVE provides non-vanishing gradient signals enabling reliable optimization with consistent improvements on classification, segmentation, and detection benchmarks.

problem: Abductive reasoning remains underexplored in LLMs; existing deductive frameworks fail to generalize, suffering from evidence fabrication, context drift, failed backtracking, and early stopping.
approach: Graph of States grounds multi-agent collaboration in structured belief states with a causal graph encoding logical dependencies and a state machine governing valid reasoning transitions, aligning focus with symbolic constraints.
contribution: GoS significantly outperforms baselines on real-world abductive tasks by transforming aimless exploration into convergent directed search.

problem: Diffusion-based neural solvers for combinatorial optimization repeatedly re-evaluate dense interactions, making inference expensive in wall-clock time and memory-bound at scale.
approach: LoRe is a training-free inference-time wrapper enforcing per-step interaction-evaluation budgeting by dynamically routing computation to high-conflict/high-uncertainty interactions instead of fixed sparsification.
contribution: LoRe extends feasible MIS inference 3x beyond baseline's out-of-memory limit with ~8x speedup and ~12x memory reduction while preserving solution quality; achieves ~15x speedup on TSP with 44x memory reduction.

problem: Multi-turn LLM agent attacks split malicious intents across turns to hide future risks; existing detection methods rely on historical context and fail to identify deep attack strategies.
approach: Speculative Safety Honeypot uses a multi-agent simulation with small LLMs to speculate future agent behaviors, building a trajectory tree to expose risks, then verifies with real actions to calibrate and reduce false positives.
contribution: SSH provides existing detectors with rich decision redundancy, improving defense resilience and warning lead-time against complex temporal attacks.

problem: Batch normalization layers for neural networks on complex domains are understudied; less-studied domains like the Siegel disk lack practical implementations.
approach: BN layers for complex domains are proposed with close connections to Riemannian BN, deriving essential components for practical implementations on complex domains including Siegel disk.
contribution: Experiments on radar clutter classification, node classification, and action recognition demonstrate efficacy of complex domain batch normalization.

problem: DICE-based offline imitation learning with suboptimal supplementary data either relies on strict coverage assumptions or requires additional regularization, limiting performance.
approach: ReDICE reformulates the DICE objective to construct a mixture-distribution objective removing coverage assumptions; its dual reduces to stable Gumbel regression, with a novel policy extraction mechanism.
contribution: ReDICE consistently outperforms prior methods on standard and real-world offline IL benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art results.
